Allocation of rice for A.P.L. families in Orissa 
3477. SHRI KISHORE KUMAR MOHANTY: Will the Minister of CONSUMER 
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state: 
(a) the quantity of rice for APL families being allotted per month 
to Orissa; 
(b) whether the quantity which was allotted earlier, was much more 
than this; 
(c) whether State Government has raised a demand to restore the 
previous trend; and 
(d) whether any action has been taken in this direction? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND 
PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (PROF. K.V. THOMAS): (a) to (d) Under Targeted Public 
Distribution System (TPDS) allocations of foodgrains, including rice, to 
States and UTs, including Orissa for Above Poverty Line (APL) families 
are made on the basis of availability of foodgrains in the Central Pool 
and their past offtake. Allocations of rice for the APL category were 
made in larger quantities till 2006- 07 in view of surplus stocks 
available in the Central Pool at that time. However, offtake by the State 
Government was low. 
In view of constraints on stock position of rice in the Central Pool, 
the allocation of rice under TPDS to States/UTs, including Orissa, for 
the APL category was rationalized from April, 2007 and again from April, 
2008 on the basis of past offtake and availability of stocks in the 
Central Pool. Presently, allocation of 12988 MTs of rice and 39407 MTs of 
wheat are made for APL families in Orissa @ 15 kg/family/month. 
The State Government has requested for enhancing the rice allocation 
to 65000 MTs. Considering the request of the State Government and 
availability of foodgrains in the Central Pool, to augment availability 
of foodgrains (including rice) in the State, the following adhoc 
allocations of foodgrains have been made to the State during 2010- 11 for 
APL and Below Poverty Line (BPL) families: 
(i) 73245 tons of rice and 42202 tons of wheat allocated in May, 
2010 for all accepted families under TPDS, including APL families. 
(ii) 126453 tons of rice for BPL families at BPL price allocated in 
September, 2010 for distribution in six months.

Computerization of P.D.S. operation 
3478. PROF. ANIL KUMAR SAHANI: Will the Minister of CONSUMER 
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of measures taken by Government to curb 
leakage/diversion of foodgrains meant for TPDS; 
(b) whether there is any proposal to computerize PDS operations; and 
(c) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND 
PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (PROF. K.V. THOMAS): (a) TPDS is operated under the 
joint responsibility of the Central and the State/Union Territory (UT) 
Governments. Central Government is responsible for procurement, 
allocation and transportation of foodgrains upto the designated depots of 
the Food Corporation of India. The operational responsibilities for 
allocation of foodgrains within the States/UTs, identification of 
eligible Below Poverty Line (BPL) families, issuance of ration cards to 
them and supervision over and monitoring of functioning of Fair Price 
Shops (FPSs) rest with the concerned State/UT Government. 
Complaints as and when received by the Central Government about 
malpractices in TPDS including leakage/diversion of foodgrains, are sent 
to the concerned State Governments/UT Administrations for inquiry and 
necessary action. 
Government has issued directions to State Governments to streamline 
functioning of TPDS by enforcing provisions of PDS (Control) Order, 2001. 
Government has also issued instructions to States/Union Territories to 
strengthen functioning of Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS) by 
improving monitoring mechanism and vigilance, increased transparency in 
functioning of TPDS, use of Information and Communication Technology 
(ICT) tools and improving the efficiency of Fair Price Shop operations. 
(b) and (c) Government of India has approved implementation of the 
scheme of Computerization of Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS) 
Operations in a phased manner to improve the efficiency and effectiveness 
of the TPDS. In the first phase, the scheme has been approved to be 
implemented on pilot basis in three districts each of Andhra Pradesh, 
Assam, Chhattisgarh  and  Delhi  and  piloting  of  foodgrain  bag  
tracking  in one district in Chhattisgarh. The  

 179 
scheme shall concentrate on key functional areas, namely, allocation, off 
take reporting, storage, movement, finance, licensing and regulation and 
grievance redressal. 
A pilot scheme on Smart Card based delivery of essential commodities 
has also been approved for Chandigarh UT and Haryana. Under the scheme, 
existing ration cards are to be replaced by Smart Cards. 
Adoption of Tendulkar Committee Report 
3479. SHRI KANJIBHAI PATEL: Will the Minister of CONSUMER 
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Tendulkar Committee has submitted its report on 
Methodology for Estimation of Poverty; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the State Governments including Government of Gujarat 
have represented to Central Government for early adoption of the 
Tendulkar Committee Report so that States are allocated foodgrains as per 
the recommendations of the report; and 
(d) if so, by when the report will be adopted by Central Government? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND 
PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (PROF. K.V. THOMAS): (a) to (d) Planning Commission 
is the nodal agency of the Government of India for estimating poverty at 
National and State Levels. Planning Commission constituted an Expert 
Group to review the methodology of estimation of poverty under the 
chairmanship of Prof. Suresh D. Tendulkar. The Expert Group submitted its 
report in December, 2009 which has been accepted by the Planning 
Commission. As per recommendations made by the Tendulkar Committee, the 
All-India poverty headcount ratio for 2004- 05 is estimated at 37.2% 
(41.8% for rural and 25.7 % for urban). 
Requests have been received from some State/Union Territory (UT) 
Governments, including State of Gujarat, for increasing the accepted 
number of Below Poverty Line (BPL) families under Targeted Public 
Distribution System (TPDS) in terms of the recommendations of the 
Tendulkar Committee Report. 
The proposed law on National Food Security, inter- alia, envisages 
entitling every family below poverty  line  to  a  certain  quantity  of  
foodgrains  each  month at subsidized prices. An Empowered  

 180 
Group of Ministers (EGoM) has been constituted to consider various issues 
regarding the proposed law on food security. Based on recommendations of 
National Advisory Council (NAC) and other stakeholders on coverage, legal 
entitlements to subsidized foodgrains, etc. and directions of EGoM, the 
draft bill on National Food Security Act would be prepared and further 
action taken.

3482. SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRASEKHAR: Will the Minister of CONSUMER 
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state: 
(a) the number of Below Poverty Line (BPL) families eligible for 
subsidized foodgrains under the Public Distribution System in the State 
of Karnataka; 
(b) whether Government of Karnataka has submitted any proposal for 
increasing the number of BPL family card holders; and 
(c) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND 
PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (PROF. K.V. THOMAS): (a) to (c) For allocation of 
foodgrains (wheat and rice) to States and Union Territories (UTs) under 
Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS), Department of Food and Public 
Distribution uses the number of Below Poverty Line (BPL) families based 
on 1993-94 poverty estimates of Planning Commission and the population 
estimates of the Registrar General of India as on 1st March, 2000 or the 
number of such families actually identified and ration cards issued to 
them by the State/UT Governments, whichever is less. As per these 
estimates, the number of BPL families is 6.52 crore, which includes 2.43 
crore Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) families. 
As per above estimates, the number of BPL families in Karnataka are 
31.29 lakh, including 11.997 lakh AAY families. The allocations of 
foodgrains under TPDS to these 6.52 crore accepted number of BPL/AAY 
families, including 31.29 lakh BPL/AAY families in State of Karnataka are 
made @ 35 kg per family per month at subsidized prices. 
Requests have been received from some State/Union Territory (UT) 
Governments, including State of Karnataka, for increasing the accepted 
number of BPL families under TPDS. However, as the allocations of 
foodgrains are made to 6.52 crore accepted number of BPL/AAY families @ 
35 kg per family per month and these norms are uniformly applicable to 
all States/UTs, the requests from the State/UT Governments for increase 
in number of BPL families and allocation of foodgrains could not be 
accepted.

Illiteracy in the country 
3485. SHRI NATUJI HALAJI THAKOR: Will the Minister of HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) the number of illiterates in each State/Union Territory at 
present, gender-wise; 
(b) whether a recent survey by UNESCO has revealed that more than 35 
per cent of illiterates in the world reside in India, particularly in 
economically backward States; 
(c) if so, the reaction of Government thereto; and 
(d) the achievements made so far under SSA and Saakshar Bharat 
Scheme? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRIMATI D. PURANDESWARI): (a) The gender- wise number of adult 
illiterates in each State/UT, as per 2001 Census, is given in the 
Statement (See below). 
(b) According to Global Education Digest, 2010, brought out by the 
UNESCO Institute for Statistics (UIS), for the reference year 2006, an 
estimated number of 796 million adults (15 years and above) lacked basic 
literacy skills, out of which 283 million have been reported to be in 
India (35% approx.). 
(c) and (d) The Government acknowledges centrality of literacy to 
development - individual, societal and national -  and is committed to 
eradication of illiteracy in the country. The National Literacy Goal is 

 188 
to raise, by 2012, the literacy rate to 80% and reduce the gender gap to 
10%, besides  minimising  regional,  social  and gender disparities in 
literacy levels. Towards this objective,  

 189 
Saakshar Bharat, a new variant of the National Literacy Mission, was 
launched on 8th September 2009 and since then been rolled out in 167 
districts. It has been decided to cover 118 additional districts during 
2010-11. 
The core strategy is to improve Equity, Access and Quality of adult 
education besides Good Governance. To ensure equity, the prime focus of 
the mission is on women, SCs, STs, minorities and other disadvantaged 
groups. To improve access, the programme provides for setting up of at 
least one Adult Education Centre, in each eligible Gram Panchayat. To 
make it participatory, Gram Panchayats, along with community, are 
envisaged as the implementing agencies at the grass root level. To ensure 
quality, the scheme provides for development of core curriculum 
framework, high quality teaching learning material, improving quality of 
literacy educators, assessment and certification, new learning 
technologies, promotion of literate environment and adequate resource 
support. Towards good governance, a web based fund release and accounting 
system to facilitate 'Just- in-time' release of funds and also robust 
monitoring and evaluation system have been devised to infuse 
transparency, accountability and organisational efficiency in 
implementation. 
Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) provides for Universalisation of 
Elementary Education for all children in the 6- 14 age group. Since 
inception of the programme and till 30.9- 2010, 1.62 lakh primary schools 
and 1.47 lakh upper primary schools have been opened, 1.37 lakh primary 
school buildings, 0.85 lakh upper primary school buildings and 9.66 lakh 
additional classrooms constructed and 11.13 lakh teachers recruited. In 
2009-10, free text books were provided to 9.64 crore children and 35.09 
lakh teachers were provided annual in- service training under the 
programme.

Growing violence among students 
3486. SHRIMATI JAYANTHI NATARAJAN: Will the Minister of HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that off late violence is growing amongst 
the college and school students of the country; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether any study has been conducted in this regard; 
(d) if so, the outcome thereof; and 
(e) the remedial measures Government proposes to take in this 
regard? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRIMATI D. PURANDESWARI): (a) to (d) Sporadic incidents of violence 
have been reported amongst various colleges and school students. No 
centralised study has been conducted in this regard. 

 193 
(e) To curb such incidents, the following remedial measures have 
been taken: 
(i) For prevention of cruelty towards children in the schools affiliated 
to it, a provision has been incorporated under Rule 44.1 (d) in the 
Affiliation Bye- Laws of the Central Board of Secondary 
Education(CBSE), which empowers the School Managing Committee to 
place an employee under suspension if he/she is charged with cruelty 
with any student or any employee of the school. 
(ii) CBSE has also issued a circular in July, 2009 to its affiliated 
schools giving clear guidelines for establishing an atmosphere, free 
from fear, in every school. 
(iii) As part of the Adolescence Education Programme, the CBSE has 
brought out a set of Training Material which enlists series of co-
curricular activities, addressed to the issues of gender sensitivity 
including avoidance of sexual abuse. 
iv) The University Grants Commission (UGC) has notified 'The UGC 
Regulations on Curbing the Menace of Ragging in Higher Educational 
Institutions, 2009'. Other statutory councils like All India Council 
for Technical Education (AICTE), Medical Council of India (MCI) and 
Dental Council of India (DCI) have also notified the anti- ragging 
regulations. Since June, 2009, UGC has also started a Toll free Anti 
ragging helpline.

DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether despite huge amount of expenditure on Sarva Shiksha 
Abhiyan (SSA), 29 per cent of people are still illiterate in the country; 
(b) the steps taken by Government to eradicate illiteracy; and

the percentage of reduction recorded in illiteracy? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRIMATI D. PURANDESWARI): (a) to (c) Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) 
provides for Universalisation of Elementary Education for all children in 
the 6- 14 age group. As per National Sample Survey conducted through 
Social and Rural Research Institute (SRI) -  a unit of International 
Marketing Research Bureau (IMRB) the number of Out of School Children has

implementation of SSA programme for each year in 2008-09 and 2009-10.

literacy data. As per Census 2001, the literacy rate in the country is 
65.38 %. The male literacy rate is 75.85 % and the female literacy rate 
is 54.16 %. To give impetus to female literacy and reduce gender gap in 
literacy, Government has launched the Saakshar Bharat programme. Saakshar 
Bharat programme focuses on women's literacy, it has been provided a 
Central Budget support of Rs. 1167.00 crore in 2010-11.

3508. SHRI AVTAR SINGH KARIMPURI: Will the Minister of HUMAN

students are on the rise; 
(b) if so, the details thereof;

and physical torture in schools, registered during each of the last three 
years and in the current year, State-wise particularly in Punjab, Haryana 
and Uttar Pradesh; and

punishment and physical torture of students by the school teachers in 
Government and private schools? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

banned in all the schools affiliated to Central Board of Secondary 
Education (CBSE). Several States have also banned corporal punishment in 
their schools.

punishment in Schools. However, as education is a concurrent subject and 
majority of schools are under the purview of the State Governments, data

Act, 2009, which is applicable to the elementary stage of school 
children, no child shall be subjected to physical punishment or mental 
harassment. The Ministry has written letters in December, 2007 and again

all schools under their jurisdiction and most of the states/UTs have 
prohibited corporal punishment in their schools. The National Commission 
for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) has also issued detailed 
guidelines to all States/UTs on banning corporal punishment. CBSE has

DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether all school children will soon have unique identification 
number after signing of an MoU between the Ministry and Unique 
Identification Authority of India (UIAI); 
(b) whether this system will help in tracking student's mobility by 
creating an electronic registry, as also among institutions imprinting of 
UID number on performance records of students; and 
(c) whether the Ministry will cooperate and collaborate with UIAI in 
conducting of proof of concept studies, pilots to test working of 
technology, process of enrolment into the UID database and identify 
registrars for implementing the UID projects? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRIMATI D. PURANDESWARI): (a) to (c) Under "Aadhaar Project" of Unique 
Identification Authority of India (UIDAI), children including school 
children, who enroll under this Project, will be given Unique 
Identification Numbers. Aadhaar number will be issued to children above 5 
years after de- duplication based on finger prints, and iris images 
(similar to adults). Their biometrics will be updated once they turn 15 
years of age. Intimation to this effect will be mentioned in the original 
Aadhaar letter.

primary/elementary level through secondary and higher education, as also

standards for recording data fields, data verification and biometric

country is at present assessed through periodic conduct of All India 
Census for the sector. The latest All India Census of Micro, Small & 
Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) was conducted with reference year 2006- 2007.

institutional mechanism both at the central and state level for 
facilitating the growth of the sector. At the central level, the Ministry 
of MSME implements plans and programmes for the development of the sector 
through its attached offices and autonomous bodies/institutions such as

of the MSME sector. At the State level, the Government assists the growth 
of the sector through the State Industry/Small Industry Department and 
its field outfit at the district level (District Industries Centre). 
There is also a plethora of other institutions/organizations at the state 
level such as State Financial Corporation, State Small Industry 
Development Corporation, State Industrial Infrastructure Development 
Corporation, State Industrial Technical Consultancy Bureau, 
Entrepreneurship Development Institute etc. to help and promote the 
development of the sector. The Government continuously reviews the 
performance of these institutions/organizations and strengthens their 
activities through new schemes and programmes and expansion of the 
network with the objective of increasing their efficacy for promotion and 
development of the MSME sector.

ENTERPRISES (SHRI DINSHA J. PATEL): (a) to (c) Khadi Institutions 
registered with the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC)/Khadi 
and Village Industries Boards (KVIBs) of States/Union Territories are 
required to create Artisans Welfare Fund (AWFs) with a view to extending 
security and other help in the hour of need to the artisans. The main 
functions of the AWFTs include providing financial security as and when 
required by the artisans on occasions such as daughter's marriage, 
medical treatment, etc. Amount accruing to AWF is usually kept in fixed

institutions. Separate accounts in respect of each artisan showing the 
subscriptions made by him/her together with the contribution made by the 
institution are maintained. Each artisan, subscribing to this fund is 
issued a pass book by the khadi institution. In the case of death of an 
artisan, the entire amount to his/her credit in AWF is paid to his/her 
legal heirs or nominees. District- wise information in respect of

Plant genetic engineering sector 
3558. SHRI P. RAJEEVE: Will the Minister of SCIENCE AND 
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Department of Biotechnology is having any mechanism to 
control the import and multiplication of genetically engineered plants 
and micro-organisms in the country; 
(b) if so, which is the enforcement agency; and 
(c) whether there is any mechanism to monitor the research and 
development activities going on in the Plant Genetic Engineering Sector 
in private research laboratories like Mahyco and Monsanto? 
THE MINISTER OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY (SHRI KAPIL SIBAL): (a) to (c) 
Yes, Madam. The import and multiplication of genetically engineered 
plants and micro- organisms in the country comes under the purview of 
Rules 1989 of Environment (Protection) Act, 1986. The Review Committee on 
Genetic Manipulation (RCGM) in the Department of Biotechnology and 
Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee (GEAC) in the Ministry of 
Environment and Forests give approval for import and multiplication of 
genetically engineered plants and micro- organisms in the country. To 
contain and quarantine transgenic material being imported by public and 
private organizations, Department of Biotechnology has established 
National Containment and Quarantine Facility at National Bureau of Plant 
Genetic Resources, New Delhi. Transgenic material imported on 
recommendations of RCGM are routed through this facility and only after 
ascertaining that the material is safe from safety angle, are cleared for 
use in research purposes. Under the Biotechnology Industry Partner 
Programme (BIPP), Project Monitoring Committee (PMC) is constituted for 
the monitoring of research projects funded in the Plant Genetic 
Engineering Sector and the PMC conducts site visits to monitor the 
progress of the research and development activities and also to keep 
financial due diligence. The applicant also makes a presentation on the 
progress made under the project before the Technical Screening Committee. 
A project has been sanctioned to Mahyco on "Stress Tolerant Rice" for 
which similar monitoring procedure is adopted.

Employment in lieu of land acquired for Bokaro steel plant 
3560. SHRI DHIRAJ PRASAD SAHU: Will the Minister of STEEL be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether the families whose land has been acquired for Bokaro 
Steel Plant in Jharkhand are agitating and demanding for employment of 
one person per family; and 
(b) if so, the action taken by Government to provide employment to 
them? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF STEEL (SHRI A. SAI PRATHAP): 
(a) and (b) In case of Bokaro Steel Plant (BSL) of the Steel Authority of 
India Ltd., lands for setting up the plant and township were acquired by 
the then Government of Bihar through a series of notifications. It was 
then agreed in principle that 'at least one member of the displaced 
family would be given employment'. As of now, BSL has provided employment 
to more than 16000 displaced persons which is significantly more than 
6019 number of families categorised as originally displaced as per the 
compilation of the Director of Employment & Training in 1972. There have 
been demands for employment from persons belonging to 2nd/3rd generation 
of land owners even after four decades of land acquisition. Some groups 
have formed different associations under the banner of which they resort 
to dharna/demonstrations from time to time. However, both the Hon'ble 
High Court of Jharkhand and the Hon'ble Supreme Court have termed such 
appointment as unwarranted and unconstitutional. In line with Hon'ble 
Supreme Court and High Court directives, BSL has stopped providing 
appointment to displaced persons. However, BSL management continues to 
provide several concessions like inter-alia relaxations in upper age 
limit and exemptions from payment of application fees to displaced 
persons, other things being equal, in employment against open 
advertisement.

Setting up of new steel plants 
3563. SHRI KISHORE KUMAR MOHANTY: Will the Minister of STEEL be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Government is considering to establish 
some new steel plants with a view to increase production capacity of 
steel; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the amount to be invested to establish the above plants and 
their production capacity; and 
(d) whether the country will be self-reliant in demand and supply of 
steel, after these plants start production? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF STEEL (SHRI A. SAI PRATHAP): 
(a) to (c) NMDC Limited, a Public Sector Undertaking under the Ministry 
of Steel has decided to set up a 3 million tonnes per annum(mtpa) 
integrated green field steel plant at Nagarnar, Chhattisgarh State, at a 
cost of around Rs. 15525 crore. NMDC Limited has also signed an 
Memorandum of Understanding to set up a green field steel plant in 
Karnataka State with an initial capacity of 2 million tonnes per annum. 
(d) Steel demand in India is growing. In order to meet the future 
steel requirement from domestic sources of production, Government 
encourages setting up of new steel production capacities in the country. 
Apart from the public sector companies, a large number of private 
investors have also signed Memoranda of Understanding with various State 
Governments to set up steel production units in the country. The demand 
position is however dependent on various cyclical and economic factors 
and needs to be assessed as an ongoing exercise and the capacity building 
is tuned to the demand situation. 
Export of jewellery by M.S.T.C. 
3564. SHRI SABIR ALI: Will the Minister of STEEL be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether £ 600 crore approximately is due to be paid by certain 
foreign buyers to MSTC on account of Jewellery exported to them during 
year 2008- 09 through Export Credit and Guarantee Corporation Limited 
under Export Credit and Export Insurance Cover;

approached by MSTC has failed to reimburse the amount due to be paid by

Credit Guarantee Corporation Ltd. to honour the Insurance facility 
extended to the export by MSTC? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF STEEL (SHRI A. SAI PRATHAP): 
(a) For the year 2008-09 the outstanding dues from the foreign buyers are 
Rs. 430.77 crore through the Export Credit and Guarantee Corporation 
Limited (ECGC) under export credit insurance cover. 
(b) and (c) Full claim has been lodged by MSTC w ith the ECGC. The 
ECGC has not accepted the claim and has failed to reimburse the amount 
due to be paid by the foreign buyers on the ground that the matter has 
since been referred to CVC/CBI for investigation.

3565. SHRI M.V. MYSURA REDDY: 
 SHRI JAI PRAKASH NARAYAN SINGH: 
Will the Minister of STEEL be pleased to state:

start Ultra Mega Steel Projects (UMSP) on the lines of Ultra Mega Power

given to Government on UMSP;

Finance Corporation.
